issues: Reward Model uses a dice icon (dice-5-1244.svg) instead of a scale icon, which is semantically wrong and misleading.
SFT Model uses a lightbulb icon (Light.svg), which is irrelevant to a language model and looks toy-like in an academic diagram.
Sampling uses a colorful dice PNG (Dice-985.png), which is visually inconsistent with the otherwise monochrome SVG icons and looks unprofessional.
The edge from Preference Data to Reward Model crosses the Training Loop group boundary without a clear visual distinction, and the dashed style is inconsistent with other data-flow edges.
The annotation 'PPO / DPO / GRPO' is placed below the Policy Update node but is not visually connected to it, making it ambiguous.
The Evaluation node uses a bar chart icon with bright blue fill (#008cff), which clashes with the muted academic color palette.
The Training Loop group is very large (560x480) and contains significant empty space, reducing visual density and making the diagram feel unbalanced.
The cyclic edge from Policy Update back to SFT Model is dashed, which may be confused with the data-flow edge from Preference Data; the cycle should be visually emphasized per the prompt.
The SFT Model node is inside the Training Loop group but also connects to Evaluation outside the group, creating a visual boundary crossing that is not clearly handled.
The Reward Model node is positioned below Sampling but the edge from Sampling to Reward Model is orthogonal and may create unnecessary bends; a straight vertical edge would be cleaner.

icon_feedback.why: Lightbulb icon is irrelevant to a language model and looks toy-like; use a neutral geometric shape or a text-only node with a subtle fill.
Colorful dice PNG is visually inconsistent with the monochrome academic style; use a simple geometric shape or a monochrome dice SVG.
Dice icon is semantically wrong for a reward model; use a scale icon (e.g., mxgraph.gcp2.scale) or a neutral shape.
Loop shape is appropriate for a policy update step in a training loop, though the fill color could be more muted.
Cylinder shape is a standard database representation and fits the academic context.
Bar chart icon with bright blue fill clashes with the muted palette; use a simpler chart icon or a neutral shape with a muted fill.
